To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neural networks with motivation (a) learn to navigate in environments with dynamically changing rewards, (b) learn complex behaviors simultaneously aimed at multiple goals distributed in an environments, and (c) generate firing patterns of ventral pallidium neurons in the Pavlovian conditioning tasks.
neural networks with motivation learn to adapt to changing conditions without synaptic changes.

neural networks with motivation (1) learn optimal behavior in dynamically changing motivational contexts, (2) learn complex behavior directed towards several goals in an environment, (3) have a structure similar to the VP, (4) can explain how reinforcement learning is organized hierarchically in the brain, and (5) can be used for the development of reinforcement-learning-based artificial agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what neural circuits can be used by animals to solve complex tasks in a changing environment.
the neural implementation of motivation in reinforcement learning.
the question of what are the mechanisms of motivation and how it can affect the learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural networks with motivation are a good model of the behavior of animals and humans.
neural networks with motivation provide a plausible mechanism for how animals can learn and execute effective behaviors in changing motivational conditions.
neural networks with motivation are a promising model of how animals can behave effectively in changing conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the motivation can change the synaptic plasticity in neural networks.
we have shown that networks with motivation are a promising framework for understanding how animals can learn to behave effectively in changing motivational conditions.
we propose a model of how the brain can rapidly adapt its behavior to varying conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
motivation is not a static variable, but a dynamic process that changes with the context.
the motivation of an agent can be represented as a vector of values, which can be incorporated in the learning process.
motivation can be modeled by a simple change in synaptic weights.
